parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
An electrochemical cell is set up as shown in Fig. 3.1.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 3.1

The relevant standard electrode potentials, $E^{\ominus}$, for this electrochemical cell are shown.

$$\text{IO}_3^-(\text{aq}) + 6\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + 5\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2}\text{I}_2(\text{aq}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) \qquad E^{\ominus} = +1.19\text{ V}$$

$$\text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Cu}(\text{s}) \qquad E^{\ominus} = +0.34\text{ V}$$
parts.text: Use this information to calculate the value of $E^{\ominus}_{\text{cell}}$. State which electrode is positive.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
In solution, iodic(V) acid, $\text{HIO}_3$, ionises as shown.

$$\text{HIO}_3(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons \text{IO}_3^-(\text{aq}) + \text{H}^+(\text{aq})$$

The pH of a $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of $\text{HIO}_3$ is $0.47$.
parts.text: Calculate $[\text{H}^+(\text{aq})]$, in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, in a $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of $\text{HIO}_3$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer from (c)(i) to calculate the equilibrium concentrations of $\text{HIO}_3(\text{aq})$ and $\text{IO}_3^-(\text{aq})$, in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, in a $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of $\text{HIO}_3$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Use your answers from (c)(i) and (c)(ii) to calculate the $K_{\text{a}}$, in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, of $\text{HIO}_3$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
The Dushman reaction is the reaction between iodate(V) ions and iodide ions in acid solution.

$$\text{IO}_3^-(\text{aq}) + 5\text{I}^-(\text{aq}) + 6\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) \rightarrow 3\text{I}_2(\text{aq}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$$

The rate equation for this reaction is shown.

$$\text{rate} = k\text{ [IO}_3^-\text{][I}^-\text{]}^2\text{[H}^+\text{]}^2$$

The rate of this reaction is investigated in a buffer solution.

The initial concentrations are shown.

$[\text{IO}_3^-] = 0.500 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\qquad [\text{I}^-] = 1.00 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\qquad [\text{H}^+] = 1.00 \times 10^{-2} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$

Under these conditions the initial rate of the reaction is $2.10 \times 10^{-2} \text{ mol dm}^{-3} \text{s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Use the information to calculate the rate constant, $k$. State its units.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
This reaction is repeated at the same temperature and with the same initial values of $[\text{IO}_3^-]$ and $[\text{I}^-]$. The $[\text{H}^+]$ is increased to $3.00 \times 10^{-2} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

Calculate the initial rate of this reaction.
